articleTitle: 6.2 GHz Lithium Niobate MEMS Filter with FBW of 11.8% and IL of 1.7 dB
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work presents a wideband radio-frequency micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) filter at 6.2 GHz that enables acoustic filters towards high frequencies beyond 6 GHz. The filter is comprised of resonators operating in the first-order antisymmetric (A1) Lamb wave mode and fabricated on Z-cut lithium niobate (LN) with 320-nm-thick suspended continuous thin film. Due to the spurious-free and high electromechanical coupling (k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) performance of the A1-mode LN resonators, the implemented MEMS filter demonstrates small in-band ripple and wide bandwidth (BW). Specifically, the measured result of the filter exhibits center frequency at 6.2 GHz, 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 11.8% (BW = 734 MHz), insertion loss (IL) of 1.7 dB, and out of band (OoB) rejection of 25 dB.

articleTitle: Revisiting Piston Mode Design for Radio Frequency Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper discusses piston mode design for suppression of transverse modes and energy leakage in radio frequency surface acoustic wave resonators in detail. Various configurations are introduced, and their design principles and achievable performances are compared. Manipulation of SAW slowness curve and use of 3D FEM are also discussed.

articleTitle: Perturbation Analysis of Nonlinearity in Radio Frequency Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper reviews perturbation analysis of nonlinear responses in radio frequency (RF) bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonators. Two approaches are given. One is based on the 1D wave theory, and another is derivation of the equivalent circuit under a few simplifications. It is shown that second- and third-order harmonic responses in RF BAW devices can be simulated well. The circuit is extended to include multiple transverse mode resonances. The circuit also works well for this case, and it is explained why nonlinear responses by transverse resonances are more emphasized than those by the main resonance. Finally, the perturbation analysis is applied to the RF SAW devices on normal 42-LT, and its applicability is discussed.

articleTitle: Laterally Excited Bulk Acoustic Resonators (XBARs): Optimization Method and Application to Resonators on LiTaO3
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper describes an optimization method for single-mode performance and suppression of spurious modes in a laterally excited bulk resonator (XBAR). The method is based on an analysis of the slowness surface of bulk acoustic waves propagating in the material of a thin plate. It was verified by application to XBARs based on different LT orientations close to the ZY cut. The simulated admittance functions confirmed low spurious modes in devices with optimized plate thickness and degradation of resonator performance with a deviation of a plate thickness from the optimal value. Analysis of the wave structure revealed its strong dependence on the plate thickness and the ratio between two components of mechanical displacement in a thin plate.

articleTitle: Analytical Synthesis of Acoustic Wave Duplexers and Multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work demonstrates the exact synthesis of acoustic wave (AW) multiplexers for the first time, building on pioneering works in coaxial cavity multiplexers. The presented approach computes the multiport polynomials composing the multiplexer and derives a set of distorted characteristic polynomials for each AW ladder filter so that they form a practically equiripple response when connected to a star junction. Each channel can then be synthesized independently to obtain the Butterworth - Van Dyke model of its resonators. This approach avoids intensive optimization procedures and represents a useful technique for the design of carrier aggregation filter modules in a direct manner.

articleTitle: A 3D Finite Element Model of H2 Emissions in Apodized BAW Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: As nonlinear emissions requirements for RF filtering solutions continue to tighten, there is a need to accurately model the general nonlinear behavior of bulk acoustic wave (BAW) devices. In particular, it is necessary to predict H2 emissions due to spurious resonances, as well as the level to which they cancel in resonators connected in anti-series or anti-parallel configurations, for example. In this case the celebrated 1D nonlinear Mason model is no longer sufficient and must be supplemented by methods that account for the bounded resonator geometry. Here we present a 3D finite element model that accurately predicts such nonlinear effects in arbitrarily shaped BAW devices, with a special focus on second harmonic emissions. Additionally, we show that the FEM model can be combined with a rational approximation method to predict nonlinear emissions based on a single linear FEM simulation, drastically reducing solve time.

articleTitle: High Electromechanical Coupling SAW Resonators Based on a-Plane AlScN-AlN-Sapphire Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work reports on surface acoustic wave (SAW) piezoelectric resonators with high electromechanical coupling coefficient (k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>) based on a-plane Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) films. The properties of surface acoustic wave modes were analyzed using finite element modeling (FEM) simulations. The influences of AlScN film thickness and in-plane propagation orientation on k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> were evaluated. Due to good crystallinity (FWHM < 1°) and high Sc doping, optimized design parameters from FEM simulations were adopted to realize a high k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> up to 5.17%, which is the highest among the reported AlScN SAW devices. These results demonstrate that the k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> can be improved by using a-plane AlScN when compared to c-plane AlScN, which is highly needed for radio frequency (RF) filters.

articleTitle: Towards the Design of Layered SH-SAW Resonators with Inherent Transverse Mode Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work we present a multilayer SAW resonator topology that enables the design of spurious free SAW resonators in multiple frequency bands, while employing the same composite base substrate. Here we specifically address the design of SAW resonators with vertical in-plane dispersion and demonstrate their ability to achieve transverse mode suppression through operating in a native piston mode regime.

articleTitle: Experimental Observation of Electron-Phonon Interaction in Semiconductor on Solidly Mounted Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of electron-phonon interaction in a semiconductor on solidly mounted thin-film lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>). The prototype is based on a shear horizontal surface acoustic wave (SH-SAW) acoustic delay line platform in thin-film LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-on-sapphire, featuring simultaneously low-loss and high electromechanical coupling (K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). A thin film silicon (Si) layer is transferred and patterned on the top of the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-on-sapphire stack. The testbed at 1.15 GHz shows strong transmission tunability under different DC bias voltages, namely 12.8 dB insertion loss (IL) contrast for 30 V static DC bias. The passband also demonstrates different bandwidths (BW) for positive and negative bias. Upon further development, this platform will enable efficient tunable acoustoelectric devices for integrated acoustic signal processing.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Acoustic Wave Multiport Functions by using Coupling Matrix Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Acoustic wave (AW) synthesis methodologies have become popular among AW filter designers because they provide a fast and precise seed to start with the design of AW devices. Nowadays, with the increasing complexity of carrier aggregation, there is a strong necessity to develop synthesis methods more focused on multiport filtering schemes. However, when dealing with multiport filtering functions, numerical accuracy plays an important role to succeed with the synthesis process since polynomial degrees are much higher as compared to the standalone filter case. In addition to polynomial degree, the number set of polynomial coefficients is also an important source of error during the extraction of the circuital elements of the filter. Nonetheless, in this paper is demonstrated that coupling matrix approaches are the best choice when the objective is to synthesize filtering functions with complex roots in their characteristic polynomials, which is the case of the channel polynomials of the multiport device.

articleTitle: Mechanical transmission loss of the sole Bragg reflector by GHz pulse echo technique with thick SiO2 delay line
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Extraction of the experimental data of the sole Bragg reflector is complicated compared to the theoretical prediction of mechanical transmission loss of the sole Bragg reflector. This is because the property of a piezoelectric layer on Bragg reflector and that of the sole Bragg reflector is measured simultaneously in the standard impedance measurement. In this study, the method to evaluate the acoustic transmission loss of the sole Bragg reflector by using pulse echo technique with SiO2 delay line is proposed. A Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.40</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.60</inf>N piezoelectric transducer whose acoustic conversion loss is 3.2 dB and fractional bandwidth is 56% was employed with two pairs Ta/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Bragg reflectors as a test sample. As a result, the experimental transmission loss of the sole Bragg reflector less than −20 dB was obtained. Experimentally extracted mechanical transmission loss agrees with the theoretical one.

articleTitle: Impact of Backward Waves to FEM Simulations of SAW Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper discusses the impact of backward waves in finite-element method (FEM) simulations of radio frequency surface acoustic wave/bulk acoustic wave devices. Owing to anisotropy of the material, backward waves not only appear at the vertical direction, but also exist in lateral directions, which will invalidate the commonly used perfectly matched layer (PML) in two directions. The ineffectiveness of PMLs may further result in inaccuracy in the numerical analysis. It is demonstrated that the infinite long damping boundary based on hierarchical cascading technique can give proper attenuation to backward waves, thus provide a possible solution to the problem.

articleTitle: A Modified H2 Emissions Circuit Model for BAW Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: We propose a modified extended-Butterworth-Van-Dyke (mEBVD) circuit to model an arbitrarily shaped BAW device’s second harmonic emissions (H2). The circuit is synthesized from the rational approximation of the resonator’s admittance. The model represents each lateral mode with an RLC circuit and a current-controlled-current source (CCCS). We validate the model using 3D FEM simulations and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Thickness shear mode epitaxial (10–12) LiNbO3 (11–20) AZO/(10–12) Al2O3 BAW resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> have been used for the SAW filters because of their high Q and k. However, LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films have not used in the BAW industry because thickness extensional mode k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the c-axis oriented LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films, which can be grown in the standard sputtering process, is significantly low compared with quasi-shear mode k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">35</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the 168° Ycut LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Therefore, the mechanical thinning of bulk LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> single crystal plate has been used to fabricate the thin single crystalline layer for BAW resonators. In this study, we demonstrate the epitaxial growth of (10–12) LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> on epitaxial (11–20) Al doped conductive ZnO layer (AZO)/(10–12) Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrate. Thickness shear mode acoustic properties of the resonator were reported.

articleTitle: Synthesis Perspective to Technology Accommodation Approaches in Shunt Resonators for Wide-Band Acoustic Wave Filters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work provides an overview of current technology accommodation approaches in acoustic wave filters. New bands for 5G-NR require extreme values of fractional bandwidths, which cannot be attained with current AW technologies. A common approach is to leverage in the usage of external reactive elements to achieve higher effective electromechanical coupling coefficients $k_t^2$. However, current designs do not control the amount of external elements. By using synthesis approaches the amount of external reactive elements can be controlled as well as choose the best option in terms of losses.

articleTitle: Interferometric investigations of BAW filter harmonic performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Imperfect harmonic cancellation of non-identical resonators in critical stages was shown to give rise to perturbing acoustic spurious modes in the harmonic (H2) response of BAW filters. We recently reported on the correlation of the H2 response and acoustic mode patterns from interferometric measurements of cascaded resonator stages [1]. In this work we expand the investigation of this approach to characterize the acoustic performance of critical resonator stages in full BAW filters during process and compare those data with H2 measurements on wafer. Also, we show that the same correlation is valid for the harmonic response of fully fabricated filters on experimental test laminates. In addition, we are analyzing the acoustic response of neighboring filter chips on-wafer to determine the nature of the variation from filter-to-filter in more detail.

articleTitle: Acoustic Wave Focusing Lens at Radio Frequencies in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Expanding techniques for chip-scale acoustic wave focusing would open doors for advancements in signal processing and quantum electromechanical microsystems. In this paper, we present a method for acoustic wave focusing and wavefront shaping at radio frequencies (RF), validated with thin-film lithium niobite on a low-loss and high coupling silicon carbide (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-on-SiC) testbed. By depositing a metal layer, we can mitigate the piezoelectric stiffening effect, and reduce the acoustic wave speed in a patterned area. Employing a design analogous to geometric optical systems, efficient acoustic wave focusing is experimentally observed. With more development, this technique could be employed in emerging acoustic microsystems.

articleTitle: Dependency of Nonlinearity on Design Parameters in SAW Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work focuses on the dependencies between typical design parameters of surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators and the nonlinear emitted signals of second and third order. The parameters metalization ratio and pitch are used as examples, but the approach can be extended to other design parameters as well. It is shown, that the interaction between the nonlinear current generation and the linear admittance is defining the measured nonlinear power signals. It is also discussed, that changes in linear properties get more pronounced in nonlinear responses. Therefore, slight effects on linear parameters will have significant influence on the observed nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Enabling Microwave-Acoustic Ladder Filters Feasibility by Bounded Filter Reflection Responses
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper explores a general ladder AW filter synthesis methodology that allows to trade the depth of the reflection zeros for greater flexibility to accommodate technological constraints. The method proposes arranging the RZs in the complex plane in such a way the device performs equiripple in band but having RZs not so deep as expected for a generalized Chebyshev function with finite transmission zeros. A validation example reaches a common electromechanical coupling coefficient for a set of resonators with an out-of-band rejection close to that achievable with an ideal equiripple response that will require different electromechanical coupling coefficient and then external reactive elements.

articleTitle: A Winding-Frame-Structure Thin-Film MEMS Resonator for Quality Factor Improvement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Piezoelectric Micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) resonators have been attracted wide interest due to their excellent properties, such as complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-process compatibility, low acoustic loss and multiple frequencies on a chip. However, it remains challenge to obtain a high quality factor (Q) because of its strong mechanical losses into the substrates. In this work, a novel Winding-Frame-Structure (WFS) thin-film piezoelectric-on-silicon (TPoS) resonator with tortuous routings is proposed. In comparison with the conventional resonators and frame-structure resonators suspended by the traditional straight tethers, the proposed WFS resonator has less mechanical energy loss into the anchoring substrate according to the effect of mechanical vibration isolation, thereby reducing the anchor loss. By finite element analysis (FEA) simulations, the anchor quality factor (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">anchor</inf>) of WFS resonator is achieved 35-fold and 4-fold improvement than that of the conventional resonators and frame-structure resonators, respectively, implying the reduction of insertion loss in the devices.

articleTitle: Generation of subharmonic responses by small particles on RF SAW resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: The paper describes the generation of second-order subharmonics from the SAW devices. The numerical evaluation of an ordinal differential equation, including second-order nonlinearity, predicts the qualitative characteristics of subharmonics generated in the SAW device. Then the second-order subharmonics are observed using a SAW resonator where diamond particles were sprinkled on the surface for simulating the micro defects. It is demonstrated that the measurement results have coincided with the theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: RF Phase Shifters Design Based on Barium Strontium Titanate Thick and Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this paper, microwave characterizations and phase-shifting applications of electrophoretically deposited thick films and sol-gel derived thin films of Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) are presented. Capacitors fabricated using Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films prepared by electrophoretic deposition (EPD) on platinum foils and sol-gel technique on platinized Si and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> demonstrate a maximum tunability of 49%, 29%, and 33%, respectively. The nominal capacitance and the microwave loss tangent are obtained from 500 MHz to 6 GHz. The three different BST films are designed to fabricate phase shifters. The total phase shift divided by the maximum insertion is 10°/dB higher in phase shifters developed with thin films on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> than in thick films. The linearity of the RF phase shifters using an input power from −20 dBm to 4 dBm is also analyzed. The linearity of the RF phase shifters using an input power from −20 dBm to 4 dBm is also analyzed. For the first time, the two methods of film deposition are directly compared in microwave applications.

articleTitle: Coupling analysis of a tunable microwave and laterally vibrating MEMS resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Mechanical resonators can be used to mediate an effective interaction between microwave and optical photons [1], [2]. To create this interaction, the mechanical resonator must be simultaneously coupled to both an optical mode and an electrical microwave mode. One way of achieving sufficiently strong coupling between the mechanical and electrical microwave modes is to use the piezoelectric effect. In this work, we characterize laterally vibrating piezoelectric AlN MEMS resonators operating at 5 GHz. Extracted parameters are then used in a circuit analysis to determine the coupling rate that can be achieved with respect to a Josephson-junction-based tunable resonator. Future integration of these mechanical modes with optical cavities will form the basis for an efficient transducer for applications in quantum information systems.

articleTitle: Application of the Input-Output Equivalent Sources Method for the Simulation of Nonlinearities in TC-SAW Resonators and Filters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: A good understanding of the nonlinearity mechanism in SAW devices is a crucial aspect in the filter stage. Nonlinear intermodulation distortion (IMD) may lead to spurious signals falling into the receiver band and limiting its sensitivity. Identify the dominant source of nonlinearity specially at high-power is important for a good prediction of the filter nonlinear response. In this work, third-order intermodulation (IMD3) products in TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated-SAW) devices are presented. Within this work we apply the previously developed Input-Output Equivalent Sources (IOES) method to compute nonlinearities of more complex structures such as ladder-type and CRF (Coupled Resonator Filter) filter structures.

articleTitle: Fingerprint imaging with arrayed GHz PbTiO3 transducers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Fingerprint readers based on pMUTs using PZT and ScAlN are extensively studied. However, the resonance frequency of pMUTs is in the MHz range. In contrast, AlN transducers using the thickness extensional mode in the GHz range are an attractive approach to improve spatial resolution. However, the capacitive impedance of AlN transducer becomes high when the size of the acoustic source is reduced. To obtain small acoustic source with impedance matching, we proposed epitaxial PbTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (PTO) transducer. The relative dielectric constant of PTO is about 80, thus the spatial resolution can be further improved. Therefore, in this study, we conducted fingerprint imaging using PTO epitaxial thin films with a network analyzer, and we succeeded to acquire fingerprint images.

articleTitle: An Electrothermally Actuated Bulk Mode UHF Silicon Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work presents fabrication and characterization of a bulk-mode thermally actuated silicon resonator with piezoresistive readout. Bulk-modes enable achieving operating frequencies in the UHF range and above without the need to shrink the resonator dimensions deep into the nanoscale. While having the potential to unlock new possibilities, thermal-piezoresistive transduction of bulk resonance modes is associated with challenges that have prevented its demonstration so far. In this work, a dual-block crystalline silicon resonator with 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> bulk mode resonance frequency of 488 MHz has been fabricated and successfully operated utilizing a 200nm × 1μm beam as its electromechanical transducer. Quality factor of 2800 and active motional resistance as low as −150Ω (motional conductance of −6.68 mA/V) has been measured for the fabricated resonator.

articleTitle: Epitaxial piezoelectric layer SMR fabricated using epitaxial sacrificial layer process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Single crystalline piezoelectric layer is expected to possess higher power durability and Q factor than polycrystalline because the dielectric and mechanical loss increases due to the grain boundary. In this study, we introduce a method to fabricate epitaxial piezoelectric layer on acoustic Bragg reflector using wet etching of epitaxial sacrificial layer. First, (0001) ZnO epitaxial films were grown on epitaxial (111) Au / (111) Pt / (0001) sapphire substrate by magnetron sputtering. Next, the polycrystalline Pt bottom electrode and the acoustic Bragg reflector based on 2 pairs of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> / Mo were deposited on ZnO epitaxial films. After etching Au epitaxial sacrificial layer, SMR based on Au / epitaxial ZnO / Pt / Bragg reflector were fabricated. The crystallinity of epitaxial layers was determined by X-ray diffraction. FWHM values of the ω-scan rocking curves of Pt, Au and ZnO were determined as 0.25°, 0.27° and 0.80°, respectively. Moreover, six symmetry was clearly observed in Pt, Au and ZnO epitaxial layers. Real part of impedance characteristics of resonator was measured by a network analyzer. Resonance peak was observed at 1.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Shear-horizontal SAW driven asymmetric structure of array gold nanoparticles for reconfigurable localized surface plasmon resonance spectrum
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Shear-horizontal surface acoustic waves (SH-SAW) can be obtained by a piezoelectric material such as 36XY-LiTaO3 after feeding an electric signal through an interdigital transducer (IDTs). SH-SAW has been used in various applications, including biosensors, physical sensors, and chemical sensors. Moreover, localized surface plasmon resonance is another interesting phenomenon (LSPR). The LSPR effect refers to the collective oscillation of the conduction electrons band at the metallic nanoparticle structure in response to an incoming light wavelength. However, the interplay of SH-SAW vibration with LSPR has received a small attention. By developing an array gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) in the middle of the SH-SAW device, we propose investigating the interaction between SH-SAW and LSPR. The SH-SAW vibration guided array AuNPs and it is resulting in a blue-shift effect with a high potential for tuning the LSPR spectrum. Finally, this study establishes a link between SH-SAW and LSPR technologies, enabling the development of an adjustable LSPR spectrum and multifunctional sensors.

articleTitle: Recent Studies on Nonlinearity in SAW Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics and Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Realization of the highly linear acoustic wave filters/multiplexers is one of the most important challenges on a radio-frequency front-end portion of cellular phone handsets, thus many studies on it, such as measurement techniques, simulation techniques, and generation mechanisms, have been performed. This paper reviews the recent studies on the linearity of SAW devices mainly performed by the authors.
